The rotation did not resolve the collision or jamming, suggesting the issue is likely a misalignment in translation rather than rotation. Since the door still jams at 16 degrees and collides with the body, I will try translating P2 in the X-axis to better align it with the body. A small translation (e.g., 0.04 m) should help reduce the collision without affecting the door’s swing. I will simulate this next.

The X-translation slightly improved alignment but did not resolve the jamming or collision. The issue may lie in the door’s orientation or scaling. Since the collision persists and the door still jams, I will try rotating P2 around the Y-axis (its hinge axis) to ensure it swings freely without interference. A small rotation (e.g., -6 degrees) should help align the door’s motion with the body. I will simulate this next.

The Y-rotation did not resolve the jamming or collision, indicating the issue may lie in scaling or a more precise translation. Since the door still jams at 15 degrees and collides with the body, I will try scaling P2 in the Y-axis to adjust its size and improve alignment. A scaling factor of 0.85 (reciprocal of 1.176, which is typical for mis-sizing) should help reduce the collision. I will simulate this next.

The scaling reduced the collision significantly (from 89 mm to 62 mm) and slightly improved the door’s swing (jams at 12° instead of 15°), suggesting the issue is nearing resolution. The remaining jamming may be due to a small misalignment in X or Z. I will now try translating P2 in the X-axis by -0.03 m to further align it with the body and ensure smooth closure. I will simulate this next.

The X-translation slightly improved alignment but did not fully resolve the jamming or collision. The issue may lie in the door’s orientation around the Z-axis, as the door still jams at 14 degrees. I will now try rotating P2 around the Z-axis by -6 degrees to realign its swing path with the body. This should help reduce the jamming and collision. I will simulate this next.

This should help the door close without interference. I will simulate this next.
